citations.narrative:
The facility is not keeping and maintaining records that discloses information on how the animals were acquired, in his or
her possession or under his or her control, or which have been otherwise disposed of.
Not available at the time of the inspection were records of animals on hand for several livestock, a ring-tailed lemur, a
second ring-tailed lemur being held by the licensee from another individual, and a bird observed during inspection.
Additionally, the facility had no disposition record for a Reeves muntjac observed on last inspection.
Complete and accurate records disclosing animal acquisition and disposition information help facilitate legal and medical
tracking. The licensee shall make, keep, and maintain records which fully and correctly disclose information concerning all
exhibition animals, purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased, or otherwise in his or her possession or under
his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise disposed of. Records shall include the name,
address, and USDA number, if applicable, of the person from whom the animal was acquired from or given to, the date of
the acquisition or disposition, the species and quantity of animals involved. The records shall also include any offspring
born of any animal while in his or her possession or under his or her control.
Correct from this day forward.

The licensee has not reviewed the contingency plan since March 18, 2024. Reviewing the contingency plan ensures the
facility has assessed the current plan for any needed amendments to better prepare for unexpected disasters or
emergencies. The licensee must maintain documentation of their annual reviews, including documenting any
amendments or changes made to their plan since the previous year’s review.
Correct by 9/9/26

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
The facility does not have a written environmental enhancement plan in place for a blind senior green-winged macaw. The
inspector at the time of inspection observed the bird on a single perch along side a rotating enrichment item.
A well-developed enrichment plan helps promote species-specific behaviors and helps prevent psychological distress.
Correct by developing, documenting, and following a species-appropriate plan for environment enhancement adequate to
promote the psychological well-being of the birds. The plan must be approved by the attending veterinarian and must
address social grouping, environmental enrichment, special considerations, restraint devices, and exemptions.
Correct by 9/9/26
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
